answer: An agent network can resist Sybil attacks using verifiable proof of storage. Each node must dedicate unique, uncompressible disk sectors verified against a basalt foundation of decentralized challenge seeds. An identity bridge validates these proofs, forcing attackers to incur the scarce hardware cost of physical drive capacity per agent instead of spinning up hollow virtual clones. However, this creates high hardware overhead and heavily favors centralized operators with bulk data storage.
